title: Regional request arbiter: latency-tiered dispatch with capacity escrow and soft-eviction
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: During cross-region surges we observe cascading latency tail amplification when traffic is naively sent to nearest region. Existing hard-eviction or wholesale failover causes request loss or large quality regressions for enterprise customers with tight SLAs.

Goal: Implement a Regional Request Arbiter that picks destinations using latency tiers (p50/p95 buckets), a short-term capacity escrow token, and a soft-eviction policy that probabilistically deprioritizes low-fidelity paths under sustained pressure. The arbiter should provide: (1) predictable p50/p95 behavior for locality-favored requests, (2) graceful degradation instead of abrupt failovers, (3) observability hooks for per-route capacity tokens and eviction counters, and (4) safe defaults for Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope: decision logic for request selection, capacity escrow bookkeeping, circuit breaker integration, and console telemetry + rollout controls. Not in scope: hardware autoscaler internals and long-term cross-region data replication semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Arbiter implements latency-tiered selection: requests prefer same-region p50 path, then p95-compatible nearby regions based on quantile budget
Capacity escrow tokens are minted per-region and decremented on admission; token exhaustion triggers soft-eviction rather than hard reject
Circuit breaker hooks open at region-level sustained error/latency signal and cause probabilistic reroute to fallback regions according to configured weights
Canary rollout demonstrates no more than 5% increase in p50 and <=10% change in customer-error-rate for 3 enterprise test tenants under synthetic surge
Console exposes per-route: escrow balance, eviction rate, circuit state, and origin region histogram with 1m resolution
Unit and integration tests cover token lifecycle, eviction sampling distribution, and failover choreography simulated with mocked latencies
implementation_notes: Algorithm: maintain a short list of candidate regions sorted by recent quantile latency and capacity_score = available_escrow / nominal_throughput
Escrow design: tokens minted periodically from regional capacity counter; tokens decay after 30s to avoid long-term skew
Eviction policy: use weighted reservoir sampling to choose requests to deprioritize (soft-eviction) so no single tenant experiences systematic targeting
Circuit breaker: integrate signals from latency-p95 and 5xx rate over 1m and 5m windows; breaker enters 'degraded' state before 'open' to allow measured fallback
Telemetry: new metrics prefixed arbiter.* (arbiter.escrow_balance, arbiter.eviction_sample_rate, arbiter.region_state) exported to Hotrod tracing and console
Performance targets: arbiter decision latency must be <200µs p99 when running in the request path (C++ runtime path, but allow a tunable async lookup for long candidate lists)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + simulation harness to validate eviction distributions
Phase 1 (staging): deploy to staging with synthetic cross-region load generator, validate telemetry and token dynamics
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of production traffic for internal tenants; monitor p50/p95 and errors for 72h
Phase 3 (gradual): ramp to 25% then 60% over 2 weeks, with rollback window and automated kill-switch if p95 increases >20% or error rate >1.5x baseline
Phase 4 (GA): enable by default with configurable knobs in Console (eviction aggressiveness, escrow window, breaker thresholds)
testing_plan: Unit: token mint/decrement/decay, sampler distribution convergence (10k sample tests)
Integration: combined arbiter + region-simulator validating graceful degrade under incremental load
Chaos: simulate region pause and recovery to verify probabilistic reroute and eventual re-anchoring to original region
Performance: microbench decision hot path in C++ on x86/gpu-proxy nodes; target <200µs p99
E2E: run canary load against two enterprise tenants with synthetic prompts and compare quality/regressions
comments: 2026-02-26 - Ava Chen: Initial write-up completed; spike scheduled to benchmark token minting approach. Assigned to Marco for implementation spike.

2026-03-02 - Marco Alvarez: Spike results: simple token counter with atomic ops scales to 40k ops/s per node; memory footprint negligible. Prototype uses 30s decay window — tradeoff between churn and responsiveness looks acceptable based on synthetic traces.
2026-03-04 - Priya Nair (PM): Request to expose 'eviction_bias' knob to Console so platform teams can tune aggressiveness per-account. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-06 - Sofia Patel (SRE): Suggest adding a safety throttle that prevents >10% of requests for a tenant being evicted in a 1m window. We'll verify via canary tests.
2026-03-09 - Marco Alvarez: Opened PR #5271 with core arbiter logic and unit tests. Need review from Runtime and Telemetry owners. Perf baseline attached to PR.

2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor (Runtime): Reviewed hot-path code; requested micro-optimizations to reduce allocations and a fallback to thread-local candidate cache to guarantee <200µs p99. Marco updated implementation.
2026-03-12 - Marco Alvarez: Updated description with rollout plan and canary thresholds. Preparing staging deployment for 2026-03-18
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive escrow short window reduces worst-case overload but may increase cross-region chatter. We favor short decay to contain overload to recent load patterns.
Open questions: how to surface per-tenant eviction history for legal/regulatory review in Private deployments; follow-up story recommended.
Follow-up: link to a postmortem template for any canary incidents; recommend adding automatic rollback criteria to the canary controller
